messages:
mike.sales: Hey team — acme trial flagged a billing/usage mismatch. Customer sees 0 USD charged in portal but their internal logs report ~82k tokens processed. Can someone help triage? :eyes:

jamal.eng: thanks — can you paste the request IDs / sample logs? is this from our hosted API or Dedicated?

mike.sales: Hosted. Customer provided two request ids: req_01H8A2X and req_01H8B9Z. They say these correspond to a big batch job that ran overnight. No error responses on their side.

dana.cust: hi all — we ran a bulk embedding job (~5k texts) and expected it to use trial credits. Console still shows 0 spent but our quota meter in-app went to 82k tokens used. Screenshot: https://i.imgur.com/xxxxx.png

jamal.eng: copying ops-bot to pull usage records. @ops-bot can you fetch usage for those request ids and the account id (acct_7882)?

ops-bot: Fetching usage for acct_7882 between 2025-11-04T00:00:00Z and 2025-11-04T08:00:00Z...

ops-bot: Found 2 calls matching request ids: req_01H8A2X (embeddings, 51,200 tokens), req_01H8B9Z (chat completion, 30,900 tokens). Total recorded tokens: 82,100. Billing status: UNINVOICED_TRIAL_CREDIT.

katie.billing: Thanks — that status suggests the usage was recorded but not applied to trial credit balance. Two likely causes: (1) the account was created with a mis-linked billing profile, (2) a race in the trial-credit assigner job. I'm going to check the trial-assigner logs.

katie.billing: quick check: trial_assigner job ran at 2025-11-04T00:05Z and returned success for acct_7882 (allocated 100k free tokens). But our metering service shows a delay in ledger reconciliation for that day. Opening ticket BILL-4521.

jamal.eng: while billing checks that, can we confirm the token accounting? For embeddings we count both input and output tokens; if they batched 5k texts and we expanded each to 10k tokens during normalization that could explain counts. Do you have the original batch size and vectorization details?

dana.cust: batch was 5,000 short docs (~120 tokens each). We sent them in batches of 100 via the embeddings endpoint (/v1/embeddings). No custom system prompts. No retries that we know of.

jamal.eng: hmm 5k * 120 = 600k input tokens — that’s larger, not smaller. Wait your reported in-app meter was 82k, so something else is off. Can you pull the raw request payload for req_01H8A2X?

mike.sales: customer uploaded sanitized payload to a shared GDrive. link: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-link

jamal.eng: grabbing it now...

jamal.eng: OK payload shows they sent 500 items in that particular request — not 5k — looks like client-side batching mismatch: they have a loop that sends 50 batches of 100 each, but a bug retried the same 10 batches 5x due to a backoff bug. So deduplicated counting will show more calls. That could explain some of the token delta.

dana.cust: oh wow — that backoff was in our wrapper. We saw some 429s during the run and our client retried with exponential backoff incorrectly (no jitter) and retried until success.

katie.billing: retries that succeeded will be billed unless idempotency keys match. Do you set an idempotency key per batch?

dana.cust: we weren't setting idempotency keys. Thought our SDK handled it.

jamal.eng: SDK retries are at the client layer. Our server will dedupe only when idempotency_key is present. So billing looks accurate for calls we processed. The other puzzle is why portal shows 0 USD charged. BILL-4521 will track that. For immediate fix we can reimburse excess trial token usage and reset their trial balance.

mike.sales: customer asks for an ETA on fix and whether they should pause tests.

katie.billing: short answer: we can manually credit back ~60k tokens within 2 hours after validation. Longer fix for the reconciliation job will be in next patch (tomorrow deploy). For now, recommend pausing automated backfills and using idempotency keys. We'll also add a UI warning about retries consuming trial credits.

dana.cust: thanks. We can pause. Can you confirm how to set idempotency keys for embeddings batch? Example?

jamal.eng: example snippet:

```
POST /v1/embeddings
Idempotency-Key: my-batch-20251104-01
{
  "model": "open-embedding-1",
  "input": [...]
}
```

If you set a stable key per logical batch the server will return the same result and not bill duplicates.

mike.sales: action items:
- jamal: validate token math and confirm exact tokens to refund (due in 30m)
- katie: apply manual credit and update ticket BILL-4521 (ETA 2h)
- customer (dana): pause automated backfills and add idempotency keys

jamal.eng: I ran the diff: recorded tokens 82,100, deduplicated by idempotency would be 21,600. So suggest refunding ~60,500 tokens (rounded).

katie.billing: starting manual credit process now. I'll post the ledger transaction id when done.

ops-bot: Billing credit of 60,500 tokens queued for acct_7882. Transaction tx_20251104_9001. State: PENDING.

katie.billing: done — transaction succeeded. Transaction id tx_20251104_9001. Trial balance adjusted to show 100k available minus 21,600 used. Please verify on your side.

dana.cust: confirmed — portal now shows 78,400 tokens remaining and 0 USD spent. Thank you! :party-parrot:

mike.sales: great. I'll follow up with a short how-to for idempotency and add a note in the POC runbook. Closing here unless anything else.

jamal.eng: filing a small internal PR to remind about dedupe in docs (link coming).

mike.sales: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
